message.value: A proxy wraps an instance, so it never sees a call to a static method. Make the method an instance method.
@Cacheable skips the body and @CachePut always runs it, so the pair contradicts itself and interceptor order decides. Keep whichever one states what the method is for.
A class-based proxy does not read a cache annotation from an interface, so this caching never happens. Move the annotation onto the implementing class.
A @Bean method returning void registers no bean. Return the object the container is meant to hold, or drop the annotation and call this from one that does.
A non-static post-processor bean forces its configuration class to be built too early, which skips the injection into that class. Declare the method static.
A component-scanned class is built before the binder runs, so its properties stay unbound. Remove the stereotype and register the type with @EnableConfigurationProperties.
Spring does not inject a static field, so this one stays null until something reads it. Take the value through the constructor and hold it in an instance field.
Use constructor injection instead of setter injection, so a built object is whole.
Reaching the container for a bean hides the dependency from the compiler. Take the collaborator as a constructor parameter, or an ObjectProvider of it when its lifetime is shorter.
@Lazy on an injection point defers a cycle rather than removing it. Break the cycle by moving the shared behaviour into a third bean both can depend on.

message.value: A singleton bean serves every request from one instance, so a mutable field on it is shared across threads. Make the field final, or move the value into the call that needs it.
Spring injects a sole constructor without being told to. Remove the @Autowired.
Spring commits rather than rolls back when a checked exception leaves a transaction. Declare rollbackFor so the failure this method announces also undoes its work.
A @Transactional that does not say whether it writes is a read-write transaction by default. Declare readOnly explicitly, true or false.
A transaction with no timeout can hold a pooled connection indefinitely. Declare timeout, raising it for the work that genuinely takes longer rather than leaving it out.
A transaction on the web layer spans request parsing and response writing, so a slow client holds a connection. Move the boundary to the service the controller calls.
A class-based proxy does not read @Transactional from an interface, so no transaction opens. Move the annotation onto the implementing class.
A bulk @Modifying statement leaves stale entities in the persistence context. Declare clearAutomatically = true, and flushAutomatically = true when the statement reads what was written before it.

property.name: message
property.value: Driving a transaction by hand opens a second boundary beside the container one. Let @Transactional own the boundary, or use a TransactionTemplate.

message.value: A generated equals, hashCode or toString over every field breaks entity identity and walks lazy associations. Use @Getter and @Setter, and write the rest by hand.
JPA needs a constructor taking no arguments, and declaring another one removes the implicit default. Add @NoArgsConstructor(access = AccessLevel.PROTECTED).
Hibernate subclasses a persistent type to stand in for a row it has not read, and a final one gets no proxy, so every association to it is read immediately. Remove the final modifier.
The provider writes a persistent field after the constructor has run and again on every load, which a final field refuses. Remove the final modifier.
A lazy-loading proxy overrides every method it intercepts, and it cannot override a final one, so this method reads empty state. Remove the final modifier.
An inner class carries a reference to its enclosing instance, so the provider cannot construct it. Declare the nested type static, or move it to its own file.
A record is final and holds final components, so the provider can neither proxy nor populate it. Declare the persistent type as a class.
A to-one association is eager by default, so reading one row reads its whole parent chain. Declare fetch = FetchType.LAZY, or FetchType.EAGER when that is genuinely wanted.
Cascading a delete across a to-many association removes rows the parent does not own. Use orphanRemoval = true, or delete the children explicitly.
A @ManyToMany held in a list makes Hibernate rewrite the whole join table on any change. Hold it in a Set.
A repository method returning Page or Slice needs a Pageable to build the query from. Take one as a parameter.

An AUTO or absent generation strategy resolves differently per dialect, and TABLE serialises every insert. Declare IDENTITY or SEQUENCE.

message.value: A proxy cannot invoke a non-public method, so this handler is mapped and never reached. Make the method public.
A @RequestBody without @Valid leaves every constraint on the payload type unevaluated. Add @Valid to the parameter.
An unnamed binding relies on parameter names surviving compilation. Name the parameter in the annotation.
A handler @RequestMapping naming no method answers every HTTP verb. Use @GetMapping, @PostMapping or the sibling that states the verb.
A @CrossOrigin with no origin, or with a wildcard, admits every origin. Name the origins the endpoint serves.
An HTTP client built at a call site carries its own connection pool and no shared timeouts. Declare it once as a @Bean and take it as a constructor parameter.
A servlet type in a handler signature ties the controller to the container and hides the value it actually wanted. Declare that value as a parameter instead.

message.value: A proxy cannot invoke a non-public method, so this scheduled task never runs. Make the method public.
A scheduled method takes no arguments, because the scheduler has nothing to pass it. Read what the method needs from a collaborator instead.
Nothing receives what a scheduled method returns. Return void, and record the outcome where something reads it.
A schedule written as a literal cannot differ between environments. Read it from a property placeholder.
A proxy cannot invoke a non-public method, so this listener never receives its event. Make the method public.
An @EventListener takes the event alone, and Spring refuses the context otherwise. Take one parameter, or name the event classes in the annotation and take none.
A listener writing inside the publisher transaction ties the two together in both directions. Use @TransactionalEventListener and say which phase it runs in.
An @InitBinder method returns nothing, and Spring refuses the context otherwise. Configure the WebDataBinder it is given and return void.
